standard_prerequisites: Same chapter: lemma-splitting-field (smallest splitting extension exists, is normal and unique up to isomorphism, source lines 2265-2293), lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure (embeddings into an algebraic closure extend along algebraic extensions), lemma-intersect-normal (the intersection of two normal subextensions in a common overfield is normal), lemma-algebraically-closed (factorization over an algebraic closure)
core_obligations: Pick generators alpha_1, ..., alpha_n of E/F with minimal polynomials P_1, ..., P_n and set P = P_1 ... P_n; the product (x - alpha_1) ... (x - alpha_n) divides P, and the splitting field K/E of P over E is also the splitting field of P over F, hence K/F is normal

Uniqueness: for a second smallest K'/E with K'/F normal, extend an embedding sigma_0: E -> algebraic closure to sigma: K and sigma': K' (lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure); the intersection sigma(K) cap sigma'(K') is normal over F (lemma-intersect-normal), so minimality forces sigma(K) = sigma'(K'), giving an E-isomorphism K' -> K
proof_roadmap: Build the candidate normal closure as the splitting field of the product of minimal polynomials
Prove it is a splitting field over F, hence normal
Prove uniqueness through the intersection-of-normal-fields argument
